claim_boundary: This artifact proves the paired diagonal bound only away from one scalar exception and compiles exceptions to continued-fraction jumps only in the strict S>>N^3 region. It proves no averaged exclusion, full paired norm, endpoint, moment, density, or intervals.

common_multiplier_scalar_theorem.boundary: no averaged exclusion of exceptional r_d, full paired norm, endpoint, moment, density, or prime-interval theorem is proved
common_multiplier_scalar_theorem.common_multiplier: in the exact Cycle-133 region, the rectangle (a+d)+c=(c+d)+a gives x_{a+d}/x_a=x_{c+d}/x_c; hence one reduced rational r_d serves every edge of difference d
common_multiplier_scalar_theorem.continued_fraction: r_d has reduced denominator <<N^2; when S>>N^3 the exceptional bound satisfies Legendre with margin S^2/N^6, so r_d is a convergent of g^d
common_multiplier_scalar_theorem.jump: the next convergent denominator is >>S^2/N^4 and the next partial quotient is >>S^2/N^6
common_multiplier_scalar_theorem.large_sieve: with kappa_d=NS(r_d-g^d), L=S/N, and distinct rational labels separated by >>N^{-2}, the paired second moment is <<(L+N^2/|kappa_d|)|E_d| up to X^epsilon
common_multiplier_scalar_theorem.residual_factorization: the paired residual factors exactly as x_{a+d}-g^d x_a=(r_d-g^d)x_a
common_multiplier_scalar_theorem.scalar_dichotomy: the diagonal target follows unless |kappa_d|<<N^3/S; an exceptional multiplier satisfies |r_d-g^d|<<N^2/S^2

remaining_target.statement: average the exceptional convergent jumps of g^d over popular differences d, retaining r_d and the original phase anchor
